item.title: Police raid JaSaD office, detain scores over alleged AL meeting
item.description:
Police detained scores of people in a sweeping raid on the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) headquarters in Dhaka’s Gulistan on Saturday, alleging that leaders and activists of the Awami League -- whose political activities remain banned -- had gathered there for a “secret meeting”, a claim JaSaD rejected.
The operation unfolded after BNP and Jubo Dal activists surrounded and entered the JaSaD office, alleging that Awami League members were holding a clandestine gathering there.
Police later moved into the building and began taking people away, turning what JaSaD said was a scheduled representatives’ meeting into a major law-enforcement operation in the heart of the capital.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police officials initially put the number detained at more than 100, although Jubo Dal leaders claimed that at least 95 had been taken away as the operation continued.
Police said the identities and alleged involvement of those detained were still being verified.
The incident comes amid intensified law-enforcement action against Awami League leaders and activists following a series of flash processions and crude bomb explosions in Dhaka.
Earlier this month, police arrested 179 people in connection with an Awami League procession in Gulshan where crude bombs were detonated.
Paltan Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Arifur Islam said those taken to the station on Saturday were being interrogated and vetted based on specific intelligence.
“Legal proceedings will be initiated following this verification process,” he said.
DMP Deputy Commissioner for Media and Public Relations Md Akter Hossain said police had received information that “Joy Bangla” slogans were chanted outside the JaSaD headquarters and that numerous outsiders had gathered inside.
Police suspected a meeting was taking place and launched a joint operation involving the Crime Division and Detective Branch, he said.
But JaSaD presented a sharply different account.
JaSaD Office Secretary Sajjad Hossain said around 350 party activists from across the country had gathered for a scheduled meeting when BNP and Jubo Dal activists entered the premises around 2:30pm.
“That is a lie; our activist meeting was underway,” he said in response to claims that Awami League members had assembled there.
“Why would Awami League leaders and activists come here? The real motive is simply to find a pretext to attack us.”
JaSaD alleged that its leaders and activists were initially confined inside the building before police arrived, removed BNP and affiliated organisation members and began detaining people from the meeting.
Jubo Dal leaders, however, claimed they had received information that hundreds of Awami League activists were gathering at the office and alerted police.
Moazzem Hossain Tapan, member secretary of Shahbagh Thana Jubo Dal, alleged that 500-600 people from several districts had assembled for a “secret meeting” intended to plan destabilising activities.
No independent evidence substantiating that allegation was immediately presented.
Among those detained was journalist Abu Jafar Surya, a former president of a faction of the Dhaka Union of Journalists.
A post on his Facebook profile said he had been covering the JaSaD meeting professionally when police handcuffed and detained him.
Police said the identities of those taken into custody had yet to be fully confirmed and decisions on arrests or other legal action would be made after questioning and verification.

item.title: PM, Saudi FM discuss expanding Saudi investment in Bangladesh
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah Al Saud on Saturday discussed economic cooperation between the two countries and the potential for expanding Saudi investment in Bangladesh.
The meeting was held at the UN Bilateral Booth (GAL-7) at the United Nations Headquarters in the afternoon local time on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), said PM’s Assistant Press Secretary KM Nazmul Haque.
During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on bilateral cooperation, trade and investment, manpower, development cooperation and regional and international issues of mutual interest.
The prime minister laid emphasis on further deepening and expanding the existing friendly relations between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia, including through greater economic engagement and investment.
The Saudi foreign minister expressed Saudi Arabia’s interest in further advancing the relations between the two countries.
The two sides also exchanged views on various regional and international issues of mutual interest.

item.title: DMP commissioner: Police negligence probe into overnight demolition of Radda healthcare center
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed said an investigation is underway to determine whether there was any police negligence in the vandalism and looting of the private healthcare facility Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur, Dhaka.
He made the remarks to reporters after inspecting the site in Mirpur-1 at around 3:45pm on Saturday.
The DMP commissioner said the incident could not have been carried out in half an hour or an hour. Based on his inspection, it appeared that the vandalism took place over a period of time.
He said the tin-shed structures on both sides of the building were damaged and vandalized, while signs of vandalism were found in various parts of the building.
Many data-related equipment and machinery inside the building could not be found, he said. Staff at the institution told police that the items had been taken away.
Mosleh Uddin Ahmed said that after learning of the incident, he instructed the Deputy Commissioner (DC) of the Mirpur division to take action.
A case has been filed over the incident and 4 people have been arrested. In addition to 1 person named in the case documents, another 200-250 unidentified individuals have also been made accused, and operations are underway to arrest them.
Local BNP leaders have alleged that reserved women's seat Member of Parliament Ferdausi Ahmed (Misti) orchestrated the incident and used police at the time. Locals have also said police were present while the vandalism was taking place.
Responding to questions from reporters, the DMP commissioner said preventing such incidents falls within police responsibility.
He said: “We are looking into whether there was any negligence on the part of our police in this matter. Since this happened late at night, we are examining whether police arrived at the scene in time after being informed, and whether there was any negligence on the part of police.”
Regarding the allegation that the incident occurred in the presence of police, the DMP commissioner said preventing such incidents falls within police responsibility, and whether there was any police negligence in this case is being examined.
He said the incident occurred at around 1:45am. Whether police reached the scene in time after being informed, and whether there was any negligence on the part of police, is under investigation.
For this purpose, a 3-member investigation committee has been formed, headed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) of the Darus Salam division. The committee has been asked to submit its report by today (Saturday).
If any police member is found negligent in the report, action will also be taken against them.
Regarding allegations of political instigation or involvement of local political figures, the DMP commissioner said the police's position is clear: no party or affiliation will be considered.
“Criminals will be treated as criminals. No form of illegal occupation or unlawful activity will be allowed by anyone. Those who engage in such acts will be brought under the law,” he said.
Asked about allegations made by local BNP leaders against a Member of Parliament, he said: “A case has been filed over the incident and investigation is ongoing. Whoever is found involved in the investigation will be brought under the law.”

item.title: UNGA 2026: Pandemic readiness cannot wait, warn global health advocates
item.description:
As world leaders convene for the second UN High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response (PPPR), health advocates and international panels have called on UN Member States to adopt a Political Declaration on pandemic preparedness.
The Friends of the PPPR High-Level Meeting, an informal coalition co-convened by organizations including The Elders, FOUR PAWS, Resilience Action Network International (RANI), and The Independent Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response, made the call in a statement on Friday.
The coalition highlighted the toll of recent global health crises, saying COVID-19 has caused at least 22 million excess deaths over the past decade.
It also said the world continues to face the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, which has infected 7,600 people and claimed approximately 3,600 lives.
The advocates said the figures underscore the need for concrete action on pandemic preparedness.
Helen Clark, Co-Chair of The Independent Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response and co-convenor of the Friends of the HLM, said the Political Declaration should serve as a baseline rather than an endpoint.
“This Political Declaration should be considered the floor, and not the ceiling of what needs to be done to make the world safer from pandemic threats, not the least of which is the conclusion, ratification and implementation of the WHO Pandemic Agreement,” Helen Clark said.
Clark urged Member States to support the text and pursue the conclusion, ratification and implementation of the broader WHO Pandemic Agreement.
“So this Friday, we say: Member States – demonstrate your full-throated support to make the world safer. Given inevitable pandemic threats, how could you choose any other path?” she said.
The coalition's call comes amid concerns over how the summit's outcome document is being handled.
Traditionally, a High-Level Meeting's negotiated text is tabled during the opening session by the President of the General Assembly for subsequent endorsement.
However, schedule adjustments for this year's summit mean the assembly will only “consider” the outcome document during the closing session, raising concerns among advocacy groups seeking clear commitments.

item.title: Ashulia factory fire: Police yet to arrest six accused
item.description:
Police have yet to arrest any of the 6 officials and employees named in a case over the September 20 explosion at the F&F factory of Pretty Group in Jamgora, Ashulia, Dhaka.
Six days after the incident, police have also yet to complete the seizure of evidence.
The explosion occurred in the Jamgora area of Ashulia on the evening of September 20. Sub-Inspector (SI) Abu Taleb filed a case with Ashulia police station the following day against 6 officials and employees of the factory.
Speaking about the progress of the case on Saturday, investigating officer and Police Inspector (Investigation) of Ashulia police station Harun-or-Rashid said: “We have not yet been able to arrest the accused. We are identifying those involved and conducting the investigation. We are seizing evidence.”
He said: “Some CCTV footage has already been seized from the factory. Several burnt vehicles have also been seized and brought to the police station. More videos need to be collected, and more evidence will be seized as part of the process. The 6 officials and employees named in the case are absconding, so they could not be arrested.”
Labor leaders have expressed dissatisfaction over the failure to arrest any of the accused.
Khairul Mamun Mintu, legal affairs secretary of the Bangladesh Garment and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre, said: “First, police filed the case excluding the owner and managing director of Pretty Group. This has caused anger among workers over the case. Second, questions have arisen over the role of police as they have not arrested a single accused even after 6 days. We want the accused to be arrested quickly. The owner and managing director should also be named as accused in the case after investigation.”
Following the incident, the Fire Service and the district administration formed 2 separate investigation committees, with deadlines of 15 working days and 7 working days, respectively, to submit their reports.
Hafizur Rahman, deputy assistant director of the Fire Service, said: “A 4-member investigation committee has been formed by the Fire Service over the incident. The committee has been asked to submit its report within 15 working days. There is still time remaining, and the committee will submit the report to the director general of the Fire Service within the stipulated period.”
He added: “Another 4-member committee has been formed by the district administration, headed by an additional district magistrate. The committee has been asked to submit its report within 7 days.”
Md Saiful Islam, Savar Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) and a member of the district administration’s investigation committee, said: “Our investigation is nearing completion. The report will be submitted within the next 2 or 3 days.”
Eight people were killed and at least 25 others were injured in the explosion.

item.title: Fire breaks out at high-rise building in capital’s Banani
item.description:
A fire broke out at a high-rise building in the capital's Banani area on Saturday afternoon.
The fire broke out at Ahmed Tower, a building beside FR Tower in Banani, around 5:30pm, said Fire Service officials.
Duty Officer Rozina Akter of the Fire Service and Civil Defence headquarters' control room said they received the information about the fire at the 26-storey building at around 5:36pm.
Two units of the Fire Service are working to bring the blaze under control, she said.
The cause of the fire could not be known immediately.

item.title: Dengue: Three more die as 1,432 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more people died of dengue and 1,432 others were admitted to hospitals across the country in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Saturday.
With the latest fatality, the dengue death toll has risen to 214 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the deaths, two were reported in Dhaka Division (outside Dhaka City Corporations) while one was reported in Dhaka South City Corporation, it said.
Currently, 5,066 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at different hospitals across the country.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 71,536 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 66,256 have recovered.

item.title: Police member’s mother, wife killed in Purbachal road crash
item.description:
A police member’s mother and wife were killed after a truck hit them while they were crossing a road in Dhaka’s Purbachal 300-ft area around 10pm on Friday.
The truck fled the scene after the incident, and police are working to identify it. The deceased were Afroza Akter Shanta, 28, and the mother of police member Mehedi Hasan.
Mehedi Hasan said his mother and wife were crossing the road together when the truck hit them. They were rescued and taken to the emergency department of Kurmitola General Hospital, where doctors declared his mother dead.
Afroza, who was critically injured, was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for advanced treatment. She died while undergoing treatment at around 3:30am on Saturday.
Mehedi said their home is in the Sridhara area under Kadamtoli police station in Dhaka. His father, Azizul Haque, is a sub-inspector (SI) at Dhaka City Special Branch.
Inspector Habibur Rahman, in-charge of the DMCH police camp, said, quoting doctors, that another woman had died at Kurmitola General Hospital in the incident. He said Afroza Akter Shanta was later taken to DMCH, where she died while undergoing treatment, and her body was handed over to the family without an autopsy.
Sohrab Hossain, officer-in-charge of Khilkhet police station, said police went to the scene after receiving the news but found no vehicle there.
He said: “CCTV footage from the scene is being collected to identify the truck involved.”
A case filed by the police regarding the incident is currently under process.

item.title: Morocco backs Palestinian state on 1967 borders
item.description:
Morocco has reaffirmed its support for an independent Palestinian state within the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital, pledging to continue diplomatic efforts to safeguard what it described as the historical and legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, according to the Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita set out the position at the annual coordination meeting of foreign ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in New York on Thursday, on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
The position was also reported by Moroccan media citing the country’s official MAP news agency.
Bourita said Morocco, under King Mohammed VI, chairman of the OIC’s Al-Quds Committee, viewed peace as a strategic choice and would continue working towards a solution leading to an independent Palestinian state within the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem, or Al-Quds, as its capital.
Such a settlement, he said, would help counter hate speech and extremism while creating conditions for peace, security and stability across the Middle East.
According to the Moroccan Foreign Ministry’s account, Bourita described the Palestinian cause as the foremost and central issue of the Islamic world and said it had reached a critical historical juncture.
He cited what Morocco described as continuing Israeli attacks against Palestinians in Gaza, expansion of settlements in the West Bank, escalating settler violence and policies aimed at altering the character of Jerusalem.
Bourita said Rabat was pursuing a combination of political and diplomatic efforts alongside programs on the ground to support Palestinians.
Those efforts include projects carried out by the Bayt Mal Al-Quds Al-Sharif Agency, the executive arm of the Al-Quds Committee.
Morocco says the programs are intended to support Palestinians in Jerusalem and help preserve the city’s historical, legal and demographic character.
Bourita also stressed the importance of collective multilateral action, saying Morocco had engaged in international initiatives aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region.
Morocco has separately reiterated at this year’s UN General Assembly that the Palestinian issue remains a priority of its foreign policy and that a lasting settlement should be based on an independent, sovereign and viable Palestinian state on the June 4, 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital, living alongside Israel in peace and security.
At the OIC meeting, Bourita said Morocco’s participation in international peace initiatives reflected its determination to contribute to de-escalation, civilian protection and conditions conducive to restarting what Rabat described as a serious and credible political process.

item.title: MCJ Club begins journey with first board meeting
item.description:
MCJ Club Limited, a newly established social club for journalism and communication professionals, has officially kicked off its operations following the inaugural meeting of its Board of Directors. Held on Friday evening at a capital restaurant, the meeting marks the formal launch of the registered entity.
The club recently completed its official registration formalities with the Office of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC).
Chaired by MCJ Club Limited President Hasnain Khurshed and conducted by General Secretary Rakib Hasnet Suman, the meeting addressed foundational administrative and operational strategies.
Key decisions finalized during the session included:
Allocation of executive responsibilities among board directors.
Finalization of general membership policies and special membership numbering.
Formation of key subcommittees to oversee club governance and activities.
General membership will soon be extended to eligible applicants. According to the management committee, alumni from recognized Bangladeshi universities holding degrees in Mass Communication, Journalism, Media Studies, Communication, Broadcast, Television, or related fields are eligible to apply, subject to standard criteria.
Looking ahead, the Board of Directors outlined plans to build strong professional networks connecting members with the corporate sector, alongside hosting social and recreational events for members and their families.
Attendees at the inaugural meeting included directors Elias Khan, Sharmeen Rimvy, Sharmin Akhter, Ahmed Sagor, Muhammad Zahidul Islam Sajal, Mohiuddin Niloy, and Shakil Hasan. The remaining members of the 13-member board—Zahid Newaz Khan Jewel, Sayadul Islam, Nurul Karim Bhuiyan, and Shahed Alam—complete the leadership team.

item.title: Radda healthcare vandalized case: Four arrested sent to jail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Saturday sent four people arrested over the attack, vandalism and looting at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur to jail.
Shah Ali police station Sub-Inspector Md Atowar Rahman, also the case investigating officer, produced the accused before the court and sought an order to keep them in jail.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Siddique Azad granted the application and ordered that the four be sent to jail.
The accused are Md Sohel, 22, Md Jewel, 23, Md Jihad Hasan, 21, and Md Rabbi, 20.
Sub-Inspector Lutfur Rahman of the prosecution department confirmed the matter and said no bail application was filed on behalf of the accused.
According to the investigating officer's application, the 4 accused admitted involvement in the incident during questioning. Information was also obtained from them about their participation in the attack in exchange for money.
However, they are not residents of the Shah Ali police station area, so their names and addresses could not be verified immediately.
The application further said the accused could obstruct the investigation if released on bail and there was a possibility of them going into hiding. It therefore sought to keep them in jail until completion of the investigation.

item.title: Narayanganj trawler capsize: Three siblings found dead in Meghna River
item.description:
Three members of a family, who sank in the Meghna river after a trawler capsized in Sonargaon upazila of Narayanganj district on Thursday due to inclement weather, were found dead on Saturday.
The deceased were identified as Samina, 17, Sajib, 24 and Samin, 5—three siblings who went missing at the time of the accident with their father Helal Uddin, who remains missing.
The divers from local Fire Service recovered the bodies from in front of Al Mostafa Factory in Boidderbazar area of the upazila between 2:55am and 8:10am, said Abdullah Al Arefin, deputy director of Narayanganj Fire Service.
“Search operations are underway to rescue the remaining missing person,” he said.
Mohammad Zahed Chowdhury, station master of Sonargaon Fire Service and Civil Defence Station, said the trawler sank at around 1:30pm on Thursday.
On information, the diver conducted a rescue operation around 4:50pm and continued until 3am.
The operation resumed at 7am on the following day, he said.
Underwater cameras were used in the search, while divers also conducted searches using various methods, he added.
Shah Kamal, inspector and in-charge of the Boidderbazar Naval Police Outpost, said the trawler carrying 14 passengers with two cows and a goat from Homna upazila in Cumilla district sank in the Meghna River during storm on Thursday.
All of them were returning from the wedding of Sajia Akter and Shishir in Haria area in Boidderbazar of Sonargaon upazila.
Later, a woman identified as Rashida was found dead during the trawler capsize while four people including Helal and his three children remained missing.

item.title: Kohli says 2027 World Cup will be his last for India
item.description:
Virat Kohli has confirmed that the 2027 ODI World Cup will be his final World Cup appearance for India, saying he is determined to give everything to help the team win the title.
Kohli, the leading century-maker in ODI cricket with 54 hundreds, has already retired from T20 internationals and Test cricket. He now represents India only in the 50-over format.
The 37-year-old has scored 14,941 runs in ODIs, second only to Sachin Tendulkar’s 18,426.
Kohli was part of India’s World Cup-winning team on home soil in 2011 and also played in the 2023 final, where India lost to Australia.
The 2027 World Cup, jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in October and November, will be Kohli’s fifth ODI World Cup.
“For me, it’s the last World Cup I’m going to play for India,” Kohli told broadcaster JioStar on Saturday.
“That is my motivation ... to leave everything out there. And of course, the goal is absolutely to win the World Cup and whatever it takes, I’m absolutely ready.”
Kohli said playing a 50-over World Cup is one of cricket’s toughest challenges, particularly because the 2027 tournament will be held outside India.
“The intensity of a 50-over World Cup is greater than anything,” he said.
“You are playing 2.5 T20 games in one day. And to maintain that intensity for 10 games in a big tournament and World Cup is a big deal. Also now, it’s in foreign conditions. It takes a lot out of you.”
Former India captain Rohit Sharma, who also now plays only ODIs, said he remains motivated by the prospect of another World Cup campaign.
“The thought will never cross my mind that the business I had is finished,” Rohit said.
“As long as you’re playing, there is always something to look forward to. And I’m looking forward to the World Cup.”
Kohli and Rohit were both included in India’s squad for the three-match ODI series against the West Indies. The opening match is scheduled to be played in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday.

item.title: Tenth woman found dead in South Africa’s string of killings
item.description:
South African police on Saturday found another body in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, bringing to 10 the number of women found dead in the municipality over the past two months.
The discovery adds to growing concern over violence against women in a country long plagued by violent crime, while police work to establish whether the killings are connected.
The semi-naked body was found near a cemetery in the Tembisa township, police said.
“At this stage, we can only confirm the discovery of the body. Crime scene management and all the necessary role players are currently on the scene,” police spokeswoman Brigadier Brenda Muridili said.
Provincial police chief Tommy Mthombeni said the victim appeared to have been stoned to death, and a post-mortem examination would be conducted to determine the cause of death.
“We have put highly capable investigators on this case,” he told reporters at the scene, vowing to find those responsible for the killings.
The nine other victims were mostly in their 20s and 30s, with some found stripped of their clothes and showing signs of sexual assault.
The first victim, a 37-year-old woman, was found naked and bound with cable ties on July 15. A suspect was arrested two days later.
Two other suspects, women aged 31 and 38, were arrested in connection with the ninth victim and charged on Monday.
Police have said that killing may have stemmed from a relationship-related matter.
Police have offered a $25,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of the killer or killers, while the Democratic Alliance, South Africa’s second-largest political party, has put up a further $31,000.
Gender-based violence is endemic in South Africa, despite years of government pledges to tackle the problem and the declaration of gender-based violence as a national disaster.
Last week, the South African government said the national Gender-Based Violence (GBV) Command Centre received 6,782 distress calls between September 1 and 16, an average of 424 a day.
That was a 21% increase from the same period in August, when the center averaged 350 calls a day.
South Africa, a nation of 62 million people, has one of the world’s highest murder rates, with more than 60 killings a day on average.

item.title: Donald Trump accuser E Jean Carroll finally gets her damages after lengthy court battle
item.description:
American journalist and writer E Jean Carroll, the only person to successfully sue US President Donald Trump for sexual assault, has received the damages awarded to her, but Mr Trump is trying to get the money back.
In late June, the US Supreme Court rejected what was thought to be a final appeal from Mr Trump against Ms Carroll’s civil claim over a 1996 assault.
It meant $US 5.6 million ($7.9 million) in damages which had been deposited by the president could be finally released to her.
But the fight was not over in the seven-year legal battle, which has turned her into the standard bearer for dozens of others who have accused the US leader of sexual misconduct.
“So I have the money in my account, and Trump goes off his rocker and tries to bring a court injunction to get the money back!” Ms Carroll told AFP.
“Why? Because he wants the Supreme Court to reconsider its decision.”
This week Ms Carroll said lawyers representing both parties had signed an agreement that the injunction was moot.
Although she can now spend the money, she says she has little need for it.
“I don’t buy stuff. I know how to be happy...I mean, you don’t really need a bunch of money now, not with the world ending,” she has said.
A second, much larger pay-out from Mr Trump to Ms Carroll is also working its way through the US court system.
Ms Carroll said the money received “is going to go to everything he hates”— women’s rights, minority rights, the environment.
Damages of $83.3 million were awarded from a defamation case that Ms Carroll launched against Mr Trump after he denied sexually assaulting her in the changing room of a Manhattan department store and called her a liar.
Ms Carroll recounted the legal fight in her book last year, “Not My Type.”
The title was a reference to Mr Trump’s infamous statement about her when she first aired her allegations.
The fight has been “hard, every single minute” Ms Carroll said.
“Some of it was thrilling. Some of it was exciting. Some of it was exasperating. Some of it I wished 100 times I wasn’t there, and some of it was very funny,” she explained.
“But it was all hard. There was not an easy moment in seven years.
“I could do it because I didn’t have children. I was older. I had nothing to lose.”
Ms Carroll said the lessons of her experience illustrated how difficult it is to gain justice and how the hopes sparked by the #MeToo movement against sexual assault have evaporated.
“No woman would want to do this now. Do you see any women coming forward?”
she said.
“We’ve seen the statistics [on convictions]. We’re not stupid. Women are laying low right now.”
Ms Carroll also offered disturbing news from other accusers of Mr Trump, who she says form a “sisterhood.”
Many of them came forward and spoke to the media or made public statements about Mr Trump only to hear him say “terrible things” about them.
“I can think of three of the women who took it to heart, have never gotten over it, and their families don’t know what to do. They don’t know how to help them,” she added.
As well as continuing to fight the defamation case, Ms Carroll needed lawyers again in late May amid reports that a federal prosecutor in Illinois had opened a criminal case against her.
“I cleaned up the whole house and washed the toilets and got everything ready because I thought they were coming to arrest me. My lawyer was preparing me,” Ms Carroll said.
After days of anonymous sources briefing the media, the US attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, Andrew Boutros, publicly denied he had started an investigation.
Ms Carroll expressed frustration at the regular threats she receives from supporters of Mr Trump, struggling to understand why powerful figures do not stand up to Mr Trump.
“I’m the only person who succeeded out of all these Americans… It makes no sense,” she said.

item.title: From foes to ‘great friends’ in a year — has China’s Xi Jinping tamed Donald Trump?
item.description:
From the moment China’s President Xi Jinping arrived in America and was personally greeted by Donald Trump on the tarmac, the expectations were set for a history-making summit.
It had been more than 60 years since a sitting US president had personally welcomed a visiting political leader on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews.
And the rare honor was a calculated move by Washington, designed to show the two leaders more as political allies than foes.
It’s a stunning turnaround from just one year ago, when China and America were locked in a bitter and hostile trade war that saw Xi stare down the tariff threats of his American counterpart — and win.
Now, Trump says the two countries have “never gotten along better” and has hailed a “truly great friendship” with Xi.
But while it may appear that Xi has now tamed the US president — known for his admiration of so-called strongmen — the description of the pair’s relationship as a “great friendship” is a wild overreach of Beijing’s position.
China does not want conflict with the US or a US intervention that would contain or constrain Beijing’s global economic and geopolitical ambitions.
But the communist superpower is not seeking a friendship with America.
For now, reading between the lines of state media, China appears to be satisfied with “stability” and buying time on issues that could put the two superpowers on a course for a military collision.
And the outcomes of this summit — or more the lack thereof — clearly demonstrate the greater US-Sino relationship is still underpinned by deeply held differences and divisions.
Both sides went into this round of talks with four great “T”s on the agenda — trade, tech, Taiwan and Tehran. They were the same thorny topics that dominated discussions when Trump came to Beijing to meet with Xi earlier this year.
But as with the China summit, little movement was made on each of these contentious issues.
The delicate trade-war truce between both nations still hasn’t been resolved, even though China would have liked it extended by a year.
Beijing made no commitments to pressure Iran into finding a solution to the ongoing Middle East war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global trade.
The US also gave no ground on arms sales to Taiwan, despite Xi urging Trump to oppose the island’s “independence.”
And when it comes to the tech industry, the two countries are both still surging ahead to win the AI race.
The absence of major announcements isn’t a great surprise — few US-Sino watchers expected any concrete deliverables to come out of the summit.
But it’s the seeming friendliness of Trump with Xi that has evoked concern, not only from Senate Democrats but from some within Trump’s own party, who are uneasy at the change in a once-hawkish tone.
Republican Senator Roger Wicker, the chair of the Senate Armed Services Committee, suggested Xi should not have been asked to visit Washington, nor hosted at a state dinner.
The lavishness of the reception from Trump is a geopolitical gift for Xi, who some observers could conclude has mastered how to manage one of the world’s most unpredictable leaders.
And while Xi may not have received everything he wanted — including the commitment to block a record $US14 billion arms sale to Taiwan or locking in a longer-lasting trade truce — the cordiality shown by Trump gives Xi a largely unchallenged path to continue pushing China’s global geopolitical and economic agenda.
Those global ambitions include a push to be seen as a diplomatic kingmaker to rival the United States, challenging US hegemony, and increasing its soft power across the globe.
And according to new research by the PEW Research Center, Americans’ feelings about China have warmed in recent years.
This self-defined success of this week’s talks also sets the stage for two potential future bilateral meetings this year — one on the sidelines of APEC in China’s Shenzhen in November, and another at the G20 summit in Miami in December.
Four meetings in one year between the leaders of the United States and China would be historic.
But pageantry without diplomatic progress is just symbolism. And there has been no shortage of that so far.

item.title: 19 killed by suspected spurious liquor in Nagaland
item.description:
At least 19 people have died across two separate locations in India’s northeastern state of Nagaland over the past two days after consuming a suspected spurious alcoholic drink, police confirmed on Saturday.
The fatalities were reported from two areas, with 11 deaths in the Tuensang area and eight in Mokokchung.
Nagaland has been a dry state for over three and a half decades, with the sale and consumption of all alcoholic beverages completely banned under state law.
Following the tragedy, the Nagaland state government constituted a special task force to trace the origin and distribution source of the toxic liquor. Local police said several individuals have already been arrested in connection with the case.

item.title: China's EUV breakthrough and the New Tech Cold War
item.description:
On Monday, July 27, the global semiconductor industry experienced a shockwave that wiped out more than $1 trillion in combined market value within 48 hours.
This panic was not detonated by an economic bubble burst or a kinetic conflict.
The trigger was a single piece of news out of Shanghai about a machine built by a company most people have never heard of, doing a job most people do not understand.
Nvidia lost roughly $250 billion in market capitalization. SK Hynix, one of the biggest memory chip makers fell nearly 14.6% in Seoul, dragging Samsung Electronics down 13.3% alongside it.
AMD, Micron and SanDisk were caught in the blast radius. ASML, the Dutch giant that controls one of the most important technologies on the planet, lost nearly 6%.
This was not the first shock. Months earlier, China's open-source AI models had rattled Silicon Valley. July 27 was the hardware half of the same strategy.
The market simply acknowledged that western export controls, once assumed to be an ironclad firewall, had failed to freeze Chinese progress.
The Monopoly
To understand why markets moved, you first have to understand what markets were protecting.
Today, almost every modern piece of technology, from the smartphone in your pocket to the AI data center requires advanced microchips.
To produce these chips, manufacturing giants like TSMC, Intel, and Samsung rely entirely on Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines built by one company: ASML.
These machines are arguably the most complex commercial products in human history. ASML's newest models, known as High-NA EUV, cost roughly $400 million per unit. It took ASML 17 years to develop this technology, creating an institutional knowledge moat.
ASML's real advantage rests not on one invention, but on an invisible empire of dependencies. The most critical: precision optics.
EUV lithography relies on a 13.5-nanometer wavelength of light to print microscopic circuits. Light at this wavelength is absorbed by almost everything: glass, air, conventional lenses.
So, the industry uses reflective optics coated with up to 100 alternating layers of silicon and molybdenum, each only a few atoms thick.
To prevent the light from scattering, each mirror surface polished to around 50 picometers, smaller than the width of a single atom.
Building these mirrors is extraordinary difficult. Measuring and aligning them is even harder.
These mirrors are produced exclusively by Carl ZEISS SMT in Germany. Zeiss mastered the process through 30 years of relentless refinement.
That is the real moat: not a patent or a clever algorithm, but accumulated engineering know-how so specific and painstaking that it cannot be reverse engineered over a weekend.
Then there is helium. If precision optics represent an engineering problem, helium is a hard supply constraint that no amount of research can overcome.
Semiconductor manufacturing relies heavily on 99.9999% pure helium to carry away extreme heat and purge vacuum chambers.
The United States and Qatar alone produce over 75% of global helium supply. In 2025, China's total helium supply stood at 5,818 tons, comprising over 4,900 tons of imports and less than 900 tons of domestic production.
In March 2026, attacks on Qatar's LNG facilities removed roughly 30% of global helium supply, and Russia simultaneously cut Asian export quotas.
Furthermore, a country cannot build a massive strategic helium reserve to ride out a war like oil. Helium cannot sit in storage indefinitely. It is transported as a cryogenic liquid.
If shipping is delayed, it slowly boils away. This means chip factories can only store a few days' worth of inventory.
That is why the Strait of Hormuz matters to semiconductor markets. Not as a shipping lane but as a chokepoint for the gas that keeps fabs running.
For decades, this is what markets were protecting. On July 27, they started to wonder whether it could still be protected.
Breakout
The answer to the July shockwave lies in a company called Shanghai Aishengna Electronic Technology Group.
Established in August 2023, this secretive state-owned firm absorbed engineering teams from state-backed startups, including Shanghai Micro Electronics Equipment (SMEE) and a Huawei-backed affiliate.
It is not ASML. It is not close to ASML. But it is the first Chinese company to demonstrate it can manufacture DUV lithography equipment at industrial scale.
DUV and EUV are different tools solving different problems. DUV—deep ultraviolet has printed most of the world's chips for two decades.
It is mature and replicable. Any serious semiconductor nation eventually masters it, sanctions or not. What DUV cannot do is resolve transistor patterns below roughly 7 nanometers. That resolution needs EUV. For two decades, ASML was the only entity on Earth that knew how to do it.
On July 27, news broke that Aishengna had successfully begun mass-producing immersion DUV machines using mostly domestic components.
Roughly five machines are planned for 2026, rising to 20 in 2027, destined to major Chinese chipmakers, including SMIC, Hua Hong Semiconductor, and ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT).
ASML ships roughly 130 immersion DUV systems per year. This is not a commercial victory against ASML, but it is a proof of concept that China can build the machine without Western permission.
The moment that proof landed, one question became unavoidable. If China can scale DUV under maximum sanctions, what stops EUV?
In late 2025, a state-backed consortium led by Huawei with more than 3,000 researchers across state institutes and private companies built a working EUV prototype in a high-security lab in Shenzhen. The market did not wait for a product launch. It priced in the trajectory: a working EUV prototype, built by the same nation that just demonstrated DUV at scale, is not a science project. It is a timeline.
That left one question the market could not stop asking: how?
The physics bet
ASML generates EUV light using a method called Laser-Produced Plasma (LPP).
It fires 100,000 molten tin droplets per second into a vacuum, then hits each one mid-flight with a high-powered CO2 laser, vaporizing it into a plasma exceeding 200,000°C that emit 13.5nm light which prints the circuits onto silicon.
China cannot source these advanced lasers. So, they chose a different path: Laser-Induced Discharge Plasma (LDP).
LDP uses a ‘Z-pinch’ effect. Massive capacitor banks dump an electrical current through tin vapor, creating a powerful discharge that crushes the vapor with a magnetic field into super-hot plasma emitting the same 13.5nm light.
ASML tried LDP in the early 2000s and abandoned it. Because the violent electrical discharge creates flying tin debris that splatters onto the ultra-precise optical mirrors, degrading them from inside.
These are structural engineering penalties that any Western fab would reject. China is not building the most efficient machine on the market.
It is building a sovereign machine, free from Western control. An inefficient machine producing 100 watts instead of ASML's 600 is an acceptable cost when the alternative is no machine at all.
The talent strategy
China is not guessing at the engineering to close this gap.
The advanced photolithography research group at the Chinese Academy of Sciences', the Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics is led by Lin Nan, previously a research scientist at ASML and its competence owner of light source technology for metrology.
Lin returned to China in 2021 as part of the Chinese overseas high-level recruitment drive— Thousand Talents Program. Before joining ASML, he was mentored by Anne L'Huillier, winner of the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Now holding over 110 patents related to EUV lithography, he and his team published research in March 2025 demonstrating a laser-to-EUV conversion efficiency of 3.42%—nearing two-thirds of ASML's commercial standard of 5.5%. The gap is shrinking.
This is not reverse engineering; it is the capture of institutional knowledge; the one thing export control cannot stop.
Bipolar tech order
China's hardware success did not happen in isolation, but it landed inside a rapidly hardening geopolitical architecture.
In December 2025, Washington launched the Pax Silica Initiative to secure advanced technology supply chains among what it calls “trusted partners” including the European Union, Japan, South Korea, the United Kingdom, and Israel.
China’s answer arrived on July 16, 2026: the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (Waico), established in Shanghai with 29 founding members including Russia, Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan and South Africa.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres attended the launch. That attendance was not accidental. It was a legitimacy signal aimed directly at the Global South.
The architecture is familiar. In the 20th century, the world divided along nuclear deterrence and competing economic ideologies— Marshall Plan or Comecon, Nato standards or Warsaw Pact specifications.
The Non-Aligned Movement tried to escape the binary. It largely failed, because you cannot run an economy on principled abstraction. The 2026 split follows the same logic through different material. The Global South has watched this movie before.
Waico has no operational track record. What it offers developing nations is not a proven alternative but a proposition: cheaper access with, so far, fewer stated conditions. Whether those conditions remain unstated once infrastructure dependencies deepen is a question Belt and Road recipient nations could already answer from experience.
But the irony runs deeper than the July crash. Washington's original export controls were designed to stall Chinese semiconductor progress. Instead, they became its accelerant. By cutting off access to reliable Western suppliers, Washington eliminated all foreign competition inside China's domestic market. Chinese companies had no choice but to fund domestic suppliers. This dynamic “creative insecurity” forced self-reliance instead of preventing it.
The results are measurable. SMIC posted record revenue in 2025 despite sanctions, and Huawei achieved a 90% domestic substitution rate for components. Furthermore, in October 2025, Beijing invoked its own Foreign Direct Product Rule, explicitly targeting foreign-produced items utilizing Chinese rare earth elements. The controls explicitly target advanced semiconductors and AI research. Trade is a weapon in both directions now. Nobody is pretending otherwise.
The full stack
This is not a chip story. It is the creation of a competing technology civilization.
China already democratized AI through open-source models like DeepSeek, Kimi and others that any nation can use for free. Software came first. Now the hardware layer has caught up. The equation is now complete.
The mathematics of the reality is clear. A developing nation no longer needs to pay Western cloud providers, license Western AI models or depend on ASML for cutting-edge chips. It can build indigenous AI infrastructure today on Chinese tech stack. The technology lags ASML by a generation but for consumer applications, public services and agricultural tools, that gap is irrelevant. For critical infrastructure: power grids, financial clearing systems, defense networks—the answer is different. No government should accept ‘good enough’ on faith when the stakes are national survival.
China does not need to match ASML to win this competition. A domestic EUV machine delivering 150 Watts of stable output would not match ASML commercially, but it would be strategically decisive. If China achieves stable EUV production by 2032, the monopoly is over. Pax Silica's leverage entirely built on the assumption that advanced semiconductor manufacturing cannot be replicated outside a handful of Western-aligned nations, will begin to erode.
The front line
On August 1, 2026, Bangladesh announced its decision to join Waico as an observer.
On that same day, a US Special Envoy Sergio Gor met the Prime Minister in Dhaka and signaled the other door was still open.
But both doors lead to dependency. That is the choice nobody is saying out loud.
The deeper question was never Washington or Beijing. It is whether Bangladesh understands what it is choosing and what it is surrendering before the architecture is locked and the choices become irreversible.
We are at the edge of the most compressed period of change in recorded human history. AI over the next 25 years will unleash more fundamental change than the last two millennia of human history combined.
AI will not change how we communicate or shop. It will change how we think, govern, fight, and raise our children. Every system being built now in healthcare, education, finance, security will be fundamentally reshaped before this decade ends.
This is not a reason for panic. It is a reason for extraordinary caution and extraordinary seriousness.
Bangladesh earned its sovereignty through costs most nations have never paid.
The question is whether that sovereignty extends to the digital layer being laid underneath every other system or whether that layer, quietly, belongs to someone else.
A government that doesn't understand what it is choosing will not get a second chance to choose differently.
The writer is a contributor and a tech enthusiast
